hints: Start by recalling what makes a lepton different from a hadron - leptons are fundamental and are not made of quarks, so think of particles involved in beta decay.
List the familiar members of the lepton family you meet in radioactivity, such as the beta particle and the tiny neutral particle emitted with it.
walkthrough:
**What a lepton is**
Think of all particles as split into two big groups. Hadrons are made of quarks, like protons and neutrons. Leptons are the other group - they are fundamental, meaning they are not made of quarks and cannot be broken down further.

**Pick two examples**
The leptons you need for AS Level are very familiar. The electron $e^-$ is a lepton, and so is its antiparticle the positron $e^+$. The (electron) neutrino $\nu_e$ and (electron) antineutrino $\bar{\nu}_e$ emitted in beta-minus and beta-plus decay are also leptons. Any two different names from this list, for example electron and electron antineutrino, earn full credit.
Final answer: 1. electron (or positron) 2. (electron) neutrino (or (electron) antineutrino). Any two different leptons.

hints: Remember the test for a hadron - if it is made of quarks it is a hadron, so ask yourself which items in the list are quark combinations and which are leptons or radiation.
walkthrough:
**Spot the hadrons**
A hadron is any particle made of quarks. There are two types: mesons made of a quark and an antiquark, and baryons made of three quarks, like the proton and neutron.
Now check the list: antineutrino is a lepton, not a hadron. Beta-plus is fast positron radiation, also a lepton. Meson is by definition a hadron. Neutron is a baryon ($udd$), so it is also a hadron. So you underline meson and neutron only.
Final answer: Underline meson and neutron only.

hints: Recall the three quarks that make up a proton and write down the charge of an up quark and a down quark as fractions of $e$.
Add the three fractional charges together first to show the total is $+1e$, then multiply by $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ to get the value in coulombs.
walkthrough:
**Write down the quark content**
A proton is a baryon, so it contains three quarks. Its composition is well known:
$$ \text{proton} = u + u + d $$
That is two up quarks and one down quark.

**Add the quark charges**
In units of the elementary charge $e$, an up quark has charge $+2/3e$ and a down quark has charge $-1/3e$. So:
$$ Q = (+2/3e) + (+2/3e) + (-1/3e) $$
$$ Q = +3/3e = +1e $$
With $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ this gives:
$$ Q = +1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C} $$
This shows the proton charge comes directly from its quarks.
Final answer: Proton is $uud$. Charge $= 2/3e + 2/3e - 1/3e = +1e = +1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
